content:
morgan: Heads up — I'm starting a canary rollout of the notify-sampling feature to cut down SLO noise from a few noisy tenants. Quick UX/API question: how should the console show why an alert was suppressed? ops keep asking for 'quota burned' visibility so they don't think the SLO system is dropping alerts.
sam: +1 need clarity. My proposal: show a compact 'suppressed by sampling' badge on the alert card with a hover detail that shows suppressed_count, original_count and sampling_rate. Also a link to a per-tenant usage view that shows quota burn over time. :eyeglasses:
jia: Prefer exposing three things in the hover: sampling_rate, suppression_reason (e.g. tenant_quota, quiet_window, adaptive_score), and the fallback_action (deliver|escalate_to_fallback). That way oncall can see policy chain.
lex: Frontend question — what telemetry do we need from the API so the UI can render the hover without extra calls? We should avoid N+1. Suggested event payload we can surface directly in the alert object:
lex: ```json
{"suppressed_count": 12, "original_count": 60, "sampling_rate": 0.2, "tenant_quota_remaining": 3200, "policy_id": "notify-sample-v1"}
```
morgan: That payload looks good. We also need a human-friendly explanation for the hover text (e.g., "Suppressed by tenant sampling — 48 alerts suppressed to preserve quota").
maria: From a product POV: add an "why this was suppressed" CTA that opens a compact timeline and a 'rollback to last policy' action for the team owning the SLO. We don't want oncall digging into infra to revert noise mitigation.
eli: We should be careful about security — tenant_quota_remaining might be sensitive. Maybe only show 'low/medium/high' or a percent to non-admins. Admins can see exact numbers.
sam: Good call. UI can show a blurred value for non-admins and tooltip that says "request access to view exact quota". Also need a per-tenant quick link to start a temporary bypass for critical alerts (timeboxed).
platform-bot: deploybot started canary rollout notify-sampling to 5% tenants (policy notify-sample-v1) — changelist CL: 4523. :rocket:
deploybot: canary rollout metrics: suppressed_rate=18%, avg_latency_impact=+1ms, error_rate unchanged.
jia: For the internal API debate: should sampling metadata live on the alert object (enriched at evaluate time) or be a separate /alerts/<id>/sampling endpoint? Enrichment simplifies UI but may bloat alert payloads.
lex: If we enrich, we need a compact wire format. We could encode sampling metadata as a small array of tags + counters rather than big nested JSON.
sam: My take: enrich with compact fields (as above) and stream full audit to telemetry/ops. UI can fetch more only when user clicks the CTA.
maria: UX detail: in the rollouts page show 'estimated suppressed quantity' per tenant during the canary so PMs can reason about impact. Also surface a small graph of alerts_pre/post sampling.
eli: One more thing — escalation logic. If sampling suppressed > X% of critical alerts for a tenant in 1h, auto-raise to fallback policy and notify tenant owner. We should surface that threshold in the policy editor.
sam: I'll draft a tiny RFC that covers: API fields, UX hover copy, admin vs non-admin visibility, temporary bypass flow, and rollback CTA. Planning to open PR with API contract tomorrow.
morgan: Awesome. Can we also add a small audit log line for every suppress action so support can answer "why didn't I get an alert?"? Even if it's aggregated, keep per-incident pointer to sampled decision_id.
jia: Yep — we'll emit sampling_decision_id and link to aggregated events in telemetry. Support can click through.
maria: Thanks all. If no objections, I'll add the hover copy + CTA mock to the rollout doc and coordinate a short demo during next week's eng-platform sync. :+1:
sam: No objections from me. Opening RFC now -> https://r.redwood/r/notify-sampling-rfc
morgan: Thanks — keeping an eye on the canary. Ping here if we see suppression > 25% for any tenant.
